# discord_application_role_connection_metadata (Resource)

Manages the role connection metadata of an application: the requirements servers can set on a linked role that uses the application, such as "has been a member for at least N days". The application sets each user's values with an OAuth2 token, and users link their account at the application's `role_connections_verification_url` (see `discord_application_settings`).

Discord replaces the whole list at once, so this resource is authoritative: creating it replaces any existing records, and destroying it removes them all. Discord's API cannot attach these requirements to a role; that remains a manual step in the server's role settings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "discord_application_role_connection_metadata" "this" {
  records = [
    {
      type        = "boolean_equal"
      key         = "member"
      name        = "Member"
      description = "Has an account on the site"
    },
    {
      type        = "datetime_less_than_or_equal"
      key         = "joined"
      name        = "Member for"
      description = "Days since the account was created"
      name_localizations = {
        fr = "Membre depuis"
      }
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `records` (Attributes List) The metadata records, at most 5, each with a unique `key`. An empty list removes them all. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--records))

### Optional

- `application_id` (String) ID of the application. Defaults to the application the provider's bot token belongs to, the only one it can manage.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the application.

<a id="nestedatt--records"></a>
### Nested Schema for `records`

Required:

- `description` (String) Description shown to servers (1-200 characters).
- `key` (String) Key of the value in users' role connection metadata: 1-50 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and `_`.
- `name` (String) Name shown to servers (1-100 characters).
- `type` (String) How a user's value is compared with the value a server sets: `integer_less_than_or_equal`, `integer_greater_than_or_equal`, `integer_equal`, `integer_not_equal`, `datetime_less_than_or_equal`, `datetime_greater_than_or_equal`, `boolean_equal`, `boolean_not_equal`. Integer and boolean values are integers; datetime values are ISO8601 timestamps compared with a number of days before the current date.

Optional:

- `description_localizations` (Map of String) Translations of `description` keyed by Discord locale, such as `de` or `pt-BR`. Values follow the same rules as `description`.
- `name_localizations` (Map of String) Translations of `name` keyed by Discord locale, such as `de` or `pt-BR`. Values follow the same rules as `name`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = discord_application_role_connection_metadata.this
  identity = {
    application_id = "456789012345678901"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `application_id` (String) ID of the application.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import discord_application_role_connection_metadata.this <application_id>
```
